stories.title: Iran sets conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz after UAE says ship was struck
stories.summary: Iran laid out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz after the UAE said one of its ships was targeted in an airstrike. Separately, Iran indicated a broader deal over the waterway is close but not yet sufficient to actually reopen it, according to Investing.com and CNBC.
stories.whyItMatters: The Strait of Hormuz carries a large share of the world's seaborne oil, so any threat to its status or shipping safety through it is a direct risk factor for crude prices and broader risk sentiment.
whatToWatch: Whether Iran and the UAE reach a formal agreement on the strait
Any oil price reaction to the standoff
Further reports of vessels being targeted in the region
questions: What exactly are Iran's stated conditions?
Who is confirmed to have carried out the airstrike on the UAE ship?
Is commercial shipping through the strait currently disrupted?

stories.title: Russia stocks close lower as MOEX Russia Index ends little changed
stories.summary: Russian equities finished Friday's session lower even as the benchmark MOEX Russia Index itself ended roughly unchanged, according to Investing.com. The report did not attribute the move to a specific catalyst.
stories.whyItMatters: Russia's market remains largely walled off from Western investors, but its price action is a gauge of domestic sentiment amid ongoing sanctions and geopolitical isolation.
whatToWatch: Direction of the MOEX index in upcoming sessions
Ruble moves alongside the equity market
questions: What is driving the apparent gap between broad market weakness and a flat headline index?

stories.title: Otis pitches itself as a defensive stock, but investors want proof
stories.summary: Elevator maker Otis is positioning itself as a defensive holding for a volatile market, but CNBC reports the company still has to prove that thesis to investors. The piece frames Otis's case around its resilience relative to more cyclical industrials.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors have been hunting for defensive names as markets swing, so how Otis's pitch lands could influence flows into industrial and services-heavy stocks seen as lower-beta plays.
whatToWatch: Otis's upcoming earnings for evidence of stable, recurring service revenue
Analyst commentary on whether the defensive framing holds up
questions: What specific metrics is Otis using to make its defensive case?
How has the stock traded relative to peers during recent volatility?

stories.title: What would it take for Mercedes-Benz stock to re-rate higher? Citi weighs in
stories.summary: Citi analysts laid out what conditions would be needed for Mercedes-Benz shares to re-rate to a higher valuation, according to Investing.com. The note comes as European automakers continue to trade at depressed multiples relative to history.
stories.whyItMatters: A re-rating call from a major bank on one of Europe's largest automakers is a read on how Wall Street views the sector's earnings quality and growth prospects, including EV transition risk.
whatToWatch: Any change to Citi's rating or price target on Mercedes-Benz
Mercedes-Benz's next earnings report for signs of the catalysts Citi flagged
questions: What specific catalysts or thresholds did Citi identify?
Is Citi's current rating on the stock bullish, neutral, or bearish?

whatToWatch: Management commentary on the drivers behind the shortfall
Analyst estimate revisions following the print
questions: What specifically drove the revenue shortfall?
Does management see the miss as one-off or indicative of a trend?

stories.whyItMatters: Network outages at major carriers can dent consumer trust and have previously pressured telecom stocks and invited regulatory scrutiny.

stories.whyItMatters: Heightened security warnings in a major European economy can add to the risk premium markets attach to European assets and could feed into calls for more defense spending.

Any broader NATO or EU reaction
questions: What was the drone incident that prompted the warning?
Who does Germany believe is behind the hybrid threats?
